Vipers #3

Tempting Venom

Rina Kent

4.32
33,964 ratings5,025 reviews
Rate this book
From New York Times bestselling author Rina Kent comes a nail-biting MM dark romance between two hockey rivals.

When two ruthless enemies collide.

My name is Preston Armstrong, and I’m the most depraved bastard you’ll ever meet.
I take what I want, ruin what I don’t, and live exactly how I please.
That is, until I crash into the force of nature that is Marcus Osborn.
Captain of our rival hockey team, and the perpetual thorn in my side.
A migraine in human form and the one person who refuses to play by my rules.
He’s my brand of heartless and just as deranged.
I set out to crush him, his career, and his infuriatingly gorgeous face.
But Marcus hits back with equal force, turning our rivalry into a violent, addictive dance neither of us can walk away from.
We were supposed to annihilate each other.
Instead, we spark a fire that threatens to devour everything in its path.
In this battle of two unhinged souls, our bodies become collateral damage.
But I never expected our stone-cold hearts to get involved.

Tempting Venom is a male x male college romance. While this book can be read on its own, for a better understanding of the world, it's recommended to read Beautiful Venom & Sweet Venom first.

About the author

Rina Kent

65 books75.5k followers
Rina Kent is a New York Times, USA Today, and #1 bestselling author of all things dark romance.
Better known for writing unapologetic anti-heroes and villains, Rina weaves tales of characters you shouldn’t fall for but inevitably do. Her stories are laced with a touch of darkness, a splash of angst, and just the right amount of unhealthy intensity.
When she’s not busy plotting mayhem for her ever-expanding Rinaverse, she leads a private life in London, travels, and pampers her cats in true Cat Lady fashion.

If you don’t know, I am one of the biggest RK’s critic. I think most of the times she is repetitive, unoriginal, leave too many things off page and her characters are mostly a copy and paste! I’ve never gave up on her books because when they hit, they truly HIT ! I for example love and adore God of Malice, God of Wrath, God of Fury, The Deception Trilogy, The Monster Trilogy and Hunt the Villain. But every other book I’ve read from her I either like it but have manyyyyyy complaints or I don’t even like it at all. Have said that I was excited about this one specifically because since Beautiful Venom I’ve been waiting for Preston and Marcus story and it did NOT disappoint it!
She finally gave me all I ever wanted in her books which is depth, emotion, all the details and complexity I was craving. Yes Preston was her usual self destructive chaotic character we’ve seen MANY times, BUT hear me out, he had many traumas, deep mental health issues and a complexity I’ve never seen in her books, I laugh with him and I cried with him, I wanted to hold him and be the mother he lost. And Marcus was everything I wanted for him, yes he was violent but he was also so caring, loving and cute, he knew exactly what to give Preston and his sadistic tendency found a perfect balance in Preston’s masochist one. 3.5 stars.

This is the epic tale of a masochist meeting a sadist and getting it on. And I mean really getting it on, like a lot.

It was so wildly entertaining that I finished it with a grin, well, until the horribly over-the-top ending that reads like a telenovela. Honestly, it had every dramatic trope you can think of, and I couldn't take it seriously for a second.

As for the plot? Let's be real, we don't pick these books for the storyline, because there isn't one, or it's so far out in the ether that it might as well be galaxy-sized. The only thing that truly matters is the chemistry between the couple. And let me tell you, this pair had chemistry in spades.

Meet Marcus, the sadist, aka the pathetic loser who's been obsessed with the fairy prince since he was a kid. For most of the book, I thought he was the cool guy. Turns out, he's just a love-struck loser in disguise.

Then there's Preston, the masochist, aka the whiny prince, who proudly declared he'd whine his way through the entire book. Spoiler: he kept his promise.

Their relationship? A rollercoaster of emotional and sexual chemistry. And the sex scenes? Oh, they were as hot as a summer heatwave, though there were a lot more than I would have liked.

It also seems Rina Kent has improved slightly at writing women; here, the misogyny wasn't as egregious as in her other books. Or maybe I just lost my mind. Who's to say?

In the end, this was a fun ride until the ridiculous ending. Because nothing says emotional depth like melodramatic chaos.

Tempting Venom is a friends-to-rivals-to-lovers hockey romance with a side of organized crime and mental health struggles. It is #3 in the Vipers series, but I read it as a standalone and didn't feel like I was missing much of anything. The previous 2 books in the series are MF.
I categorically can’t understand this man. At all. If I were him, I would’ve gotten rid of me ages ago. And yet even as he sees me at my lowest, at my most shameful moment, he’s not running away. If anything, he seems…fascinated. Enamored. And that look scares the shit out of me. Because I think I could get used to it.

Marcus and Preston are star-crossed lovers who grew up on opposite sides of the river. Marcus grew up poor but loved, while Preston's childhood was a nightmare uncushioned by his family's wealth and influence. The two play for rival hockey teams, which is relevant only because it forces some proximity and some hot, sweaty checking into the boards.
for the first time in my life, I close my eyes, burrowing my head against someone’s heartbeat instead of my own demons. This will end badly. But just for now, I don’t give a fuck.

I enjoyed the book, despite some similarities to Rina's other MM books. I'd really like her next book to skip the somewhat repetitively tedious internalized homophobia and give us a different type of conflict for a change. I did appreciate that it was shorter in this book than in others, but it felt like the same old thing. I love biawakening, but it would be nice to shift a little for the next book. The nicknames and the banter were excellent as always, and two unhinged, possessive MCs is always super enjoyable. I was having a solid 4 star reading experience up until the last 10% of the book. There was a lot of exposition packed into the end of the book and it felt like it was told to us rather than the characters organically opening up and sharing with each other. I understand why Rina structured the plot that way, but it felt like things veered off track from hockey and the MCs relationship to a great deal of other stuff that I personally didn't find as interesting.

rina kent mm romance starter pack:

—꒰ 🐍 ꒱ the characters

⊹ the top: a bold, aggressive guy who knows what he wants.
⊹ the bottom: a guy who is in total denial about his sexuality and hates being called gay.

—꒰ 🐍 ꒱ the plot

⊹ the hate: the two guys absolutely cannot stand each other. they bicker constantly.

⊹ the personal space: the top constantly invades the bottom's personal space, looming over him and bluntly telling him, "i’m going to fuck you."

⊹ the denial: the bottom pushes him away, shouting that he isn’t gay and demanding the top stop saying those things. the top ignores the rejection and gets even closer.

⊹ the turning point: one day, things get heated and they start dry humping. the top calls him "baby" to taunt him. the bottom snaps, "don't call me that!" in that moment, the top realizes he’s actually fallen in love with him.

⊹ the happy ending: the bottom finally stops fighting his feelings and falls for the top, too. they end up together.

—꒰ 🐍 ꒱ bonus features

⊹ narrator: the entire story is told by the voice of teddy hamilton.

⊹ the gold pack: the bottom has a mentally unstable mother who eventually kills herself, adding extra drama and trauma to his backstory.

“I want to wake up every day and see your face beside me and be grateful you’re right here, that you’re choosing me over your demons and whatever tries to drag you under. And I want to spend the rest of my life shielding you from any that dares to come for you. Even the ones inside your head.”

“Thank you,” he murmurs against my mouth, “for looking past the mess and not running. For letting me love you the way I know how. You have me. All of me.”

”I never imagined how healing it could be to enjoy something that ruined my life, knowing I had the power to stop it.”

November 21, 2026
Imagine being so otherworldly beautiful, that you get mistaken for a fairy prince. That was Marcus first impression of Preston and 15 years later he is still enchanted by his beauty.

In the previous books Preston was a goofball, always joking around and lighting up the mood of his friends but now we get to see a different side of him. He is hurting so deeply, spiralling and surviving the only way he knows how.

”I only ever feel like I exist when I'm being hurt.
When the pain registers, adrenaline fires. A hit, a crash, a bruise, and suddenly, I'm back in my body again instead of floating ten feet above it like a malfunctioning ghost.”

The more insight we gained into his past, the more I just wanted to hug and protect him. He is constantly battling with himself, fighting demons no one can see. It is a long journey to happiness but I was rooting for him every step of the way.

Marcus grew up with his single mother in a small house away from the corrupt society his father is a part of. All his life he was the unwanted son and that was totally fine by him. Now that his father is in need of a heir, he sees that as his chance to destroy his father’s legacy. What he didn’t plan for however is the force that is Preston.
The otherwise logical and goal oriented Marcus can’t help but be completely infatuated with the fairy prince he met as a child.

They started off as hockey rivals but of course that lead to something more. And let me tell you these two have insane chemistry. I could not get enough of them!! Seriously they are so down bad and needy and obsessed with each other. Ughh it’s maddening.

”Because fuck. I've never hit someone this... way. Like I want to fuck them into the tree while I'm beating them to within an inch of their lives.”

Preston struggles with understanding and expressing his emotions but Marcus can read him so well. He is patient but also knows how to challenge him without taking it too far. And Preston can deny his attraction all he wants but his jealousy is speaking volumes. Oh and don’t get me started on his tamper tantrums.

Marcus affection and care is monumental in his healing journey. Preston doesn’t understand how someone could be interested in him because he only sees the broken parts of himself. He is scared, he tries everything in his power to push him away but Marcus does not give up.

”Why does he love touching me when my own skin creeps me out? It doesn't even feel like it's mine half the time, so why does he look at me as if I'm whole?”

I loved seeing these two finding their happiness, although I was expecting a bit more from the vencor storyline. The story takes place in the same timeframe as the previous book. Despite knowing what was to come, it still had a lot of emotional impact. My main issue was that the early on established goals/problems of the characters dissolved way too easily or were simply dropped. It’s more of a character focused story, which is fine, just not what I originally expected.

Last but not least, I always appreciate supporting side characters, which this book had plenty of. Preston’s friend ground always had his back no matter what and Marcus mum is an absolute queen!
——————-

It’s been a while since I read an MM sports romance. Marcus and Preston’s story has been hinted at so much in the last book, I’m really excited to finally hear their full story.

LISTEN TO ME, OH MY GOD. Is it just me or do Rina Kent’s MM books keep getting better and better?! Because GAAAAAHHHHH Marcus and Preston are my absolute babies and I am completely SPEECHLESS! I have a total boatload of thoughts screaming in my head that I cannot even begin to describe—nothing but pure, unadulterated, incredible vibes! I literally gatekept myself and delayed finishing this book for a WHOLE WEEK just so I could keep these two fresh in my mind because they are now living completely RENT FREE in my brain!

Preston is our chaotic, unhinged ragebait baby who is giving us that elite, Nikolai-level pure chaos energy that I am completely down bad for. And Marcus?! The silent but deadly hockey captain hottie who is ALSO a mechanic and—IT GETS BETTER BABES—HE. ACTUALLY. RIDES. A. MOTORCYCLE. I am flat on the floor panting because that level of raw male hotness is absolutely lethal! Am I weak for biker guys? YES. YES I AM. SUE ME! LMAO.

The absolute micro-tropes in Tempting Venom are giving pure, unhinged perfection. When Marcus called Preston his "FAIRY PRINCE"?! AHHHHHH I nearly passed out from the cuteness! It was instant love at sight for both of them, masked behind the most delicious, toxic, explosive rivals-to-lovers dynamic you will ever read in a dark hockey romance. I was listening to the audiobook for this because I needed them speaking directly into my ears—which was absolutely DELICIOUS by the way—and it completely elevated the entire reading experience. Hearing Marcus {JF Harding} growl out: "You're mine, Fairy Prince. Every filthy, chaotic inch of you belongs to me, so stop fighting it," in that deep, gravelly voice?! I WAS DECEASED, GONE, SENT TO THE AFTERLIFE!

But can we please talk about the absolute world-shattering, jaw-dropping PLOT TWIST?! PATIENT X IS ACTUALLY CYRUS! What?! When that reveal dropped, my jaw hit the floor. I was standing at a literal bus stop looking shocked to the absolute moon, and the people around me probably thought I was losing my mind!

This book is a primal, high-stakes dance of mutual obsession and severe bi-awakening that completely redefines the Vipers series. Rina Kent weaves an incredibly intricate parallel storyline that crosses over with past books, making the world-building feel beautifully complete yet devastatingly addictive. The sheer gravity of Marcus and Preston’s toxic chemistry completely ruined my standards for any other couple this year. It is dark, dangerous, fiercely emotional, and the kind of book that leaves your soul totally famished for more.

Right now, I am so incredibly excited for Crave the Villain! The title alone is an absolute promise because I am already craving that villain so hard it hurts. I am actively trying to build a time machine just so I can skip straight to the future on March 17, 2027, just to get my hands on Cyrus's book and have my absolute fill of him! If Goodreads would let me, I would break the rating system and give this a literal infinity star rating! FEED ME RINA KENT BOOKS PERMANENTLY!

oh boyyyy,

i really enjoyed this book.

preston, preston, preston.

what a freaking ride.

might be my favourite rina MC of all time to be quite honest.

now let me preface this review by saying i did not read the first two books, nor will i ever read the first two. i have no interest in reading rina's MF writing, but her MM is a whole different story.

i read a big reddit thread about the first two books that grace sent over and tbh whilst reading TV, i didn't feel like i was missing too much context? sure, maybe the overarching story was a little stilted in points, presumably needing the first two books to fill it in a bit more, but honestly it wasn't that awkward.

now, as with most of rina's book, we tend to focus more on the characters and the fucking rather than the plot.

ok but seriously, is there any point of them playing hockey? they don't play... and if they do, it's described as having happened off page. what is the point of the hockey, it's not a serious plot point, and i think actually makes the book worse because i was thinking 'why is this a hockey book' the whole time.

(i didn't read the first two, so maybe the hockey part of the books made more sense because of them lol)

preston

i will protect this motherfucker with my life, i will fight for him, i will make sure no one ever hurts him again. preston was incredible. not only like laugh out loud funny, but also the depth to his character was remarkable. his upbringing was so upsetting, and what happened to him reprehensible and yet he was still so capable of love and vulnerability (albeit it took some work to get there). and his relationship with his sister was so cute agh!

(also i loved his murderous streak heheheheheh)

marcus

sure i didn't love marcus as much as preston, but he loves preston and therefore i have to love him. they're kinda perfect for one another and i can't really fault marcus for trying. i just felt like marcus' character wasn't as developed as preston? i guess i hope that's because we will see more of him in later books (ahem crave the villian ahem cyrus ahem).

all the stuff with his father, sister serena and becoming a part of vencor wasn't concluded at all. and that was a little confusing, but as with a lot of rina's books, they're all related in some respect and i'm just hoping that we will see these plot lines explored in further books, so i'm not that mad about it! (although i will be if they're just left hanging).

i have to say there were still far too many moments that were described to us as having happened instead of depicting on the page (as is the classic problem in rina's books). for example, all the cute bonding moments with marcus' mother, and as a result marcus and preston bonding and just like being together? i wish we had that more. it was the same with vaughn and yulien, i feel like rina thinks we won't appreciate the domestic boys or that we might find it boring, but honestly that's what i wanted to read more, them just doing life together instead of the constant drama and fucking. and i felt like we hadn't see preston and marcus being a couple at all, and then it's like oh it's been two weeks of seeing preston every day and i'm like ohh... i wanted to see that, i wanted to see preston and marcus being a normal couple (as normal as two psychopaths can be).

regardless, preferred this book to hunt the villain, was pretty equal with kiss the villain and didn't like it as much as god of fury!!

********************************************************
